hints: Focus on what heating does to a Group 2 carbonate, think about thermal decomposition and what solid is left behind.
Crucible R no longer contains $\text{MgCO}_3$ after strong heating, it contains magnesium oxide, $\text{MgO}$, while S still contains carbonate.
Recall which reaction with dilute acid gives $\text{CO}_2$ gas, a carbonate plus acid or an oxide plus acid, then compare R and S.
walkthrough:
**Identify what is in each crucible before acid is added**

Heating to constant mass means complete thermal decomposition. R has been fully decomposed, S has not.

Chemical equation for R on heating:
$$\text{MgCO}_3(s) \rightarrow \text{MgO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$$

**React the residue in R with dilute acid**

R now contains only $\text{MgO}$, a basic oxide. It neutralises acid to make salt and water only, so no bubbles of gas form.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{MgO}(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$$

**React the unheated solid in S with dilute acid**

S still contains $\text{MgCO}_3$. All carbonates react with dilute acids to give effervescence of carbon dioxide.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{MgCO}_3(s) + 2\text{HCl}(aq) \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{CO}_2(g)$$

**Conclude the observations**

R gives no gas, S gives gas produced. This matches the no gas plus gas combination.

options.A: Incorrect. S does give $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{MgCO}_3$ plus acid, but R no longer contains carbonate after complete decomposition, so R cannot give $\text{CO}_2$.
options.B: Incorrect and reversed. Students choosing this forget that heating drives off $\text{CO}_2$ already, leaving $\text{MgO}$ which gives no gas with acid, while the unheated carbonate is the one that still effervesces.
options.C: Correct. R contains $\text{MgO}$ after $\text{MgCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgO} + \text{CO}_2$, so $\text{MgO} + 2\text{HCl}$ gives only salt and water with no gas. S still contains $\text{MgCO}_3$, so $\text{MgCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl}$ gives effervescence of $\text{CO}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. While R correctly shows no gas, S must show gas because unheated $\text{MgCO}_3$ is a carbonate and carbonates always release $\text{CO}_2$ with dilute $\text{HCl}$.
